long_biography.plain_text:
Architecture was central to Macklowe's strategy from the start of his property career in 1960. Instead of separating development from design and operations, he assembled expertise across planning, site acquisition, building, finance and management. This model built Macklowe Properties into a vertically integrated business able to assemble sites, reposition existing buildings and manage projects from concept through leasing.

Macklowe remains the company's chief executive and continues to frame real estate as a long-term design and operating discipline. In 2022, the New York Landmarks Conservancy gave him its Chairman's Award for work enhancing the city's built environment. The recognition also reflected a broader preservation record that included a Lucy G. Moses Preservation Award.
